title: Zul'Drak
body: Zul'Drak is the heartland of the Drakkari, a vast temple city of ziggurats, walls and aqueducts climbing in great tiers, with Gundrak, the capital of their empire, at its heart. The empire is dying. The Scourge presses in from every side, raising necropolises over the lower tiers, and in their desperation the Drakkari have turned on their own animal gods, slaying them at their altars so their prophets may drink the gods' power. Between the two stand the Argent Crusade and the death knights of the Ebon Blade.

title: The Argent Stand
body: The Argent Stand is the Argent Crusade's stronghold in the lower city, a terrace above a courtyard where the fighting against the Scourge never ends, held between the Scourge on one side and the Drakkari rituals on the other. A Zandalari hexxer counsels its commanders, and the old orc Eitrigg stands among them. To the southeast lies Kolramas, a necropolis the Drakkari somehow brought down out of the sky, its wreck still full of nerubians and strewn with saronite.

parts.body: Saronite from the fallen necropolis was put to the test: an axe failed to scratch it, the elements and nature could not touch it, and the Light knocked them all back. Its secrets must be unlocked before it is too late.

title: Light's Breach
body: Light's Breach is an Argent Crusade camp southwest of the Argent Stand, raised among ruins where every troll is dead or fled, cut off from the Stand by the Scourge. Wolvar of the Rageclaw tribe shelter there with their pups: for thousands of years they lived beside the Drakkari as allies, until the trolls fell on their den to the southeast.

parts.body: The attack was no troll quarrel. Orders above an altar in the den came from Drakuru himself: the Lich King had given him full control of the Scourge's armies in Zul'Drak, and everything was to die.

title: The Dead Fields
body: The Dead Fields stretch north of Light's Breach, and the Scourge runs them as a factory: corpses lie in rows, banshees drift overhead, and the dead of Zul'Drak are gathered to be sent up to the necropolis Zeramas and made into Scourge. A Crusade forward camp on its border was overrun by them. Northwest of it lies Thrym's End, a base of the Scourge's vargul, where the king of the storm giants rages in a hundred-foot cage.

parts.body: The storm giant king came at a cry for help from his brother, only to find it a trap: his brother is now an undead servant of the Lich King, and the Scourge stitches the corpses of his people into flesh giants.

title: Ebon Watch
body: Ebon Watch is the camp of the Knights of the Ebon Blade in western Zul'Drak, raised to hunt the Scourge they once served. Stefan Vadu commands it, holding that none know the Scourge better than death knights and that the best weapon against fire is fire; he has little patience for the Argent Crusade, late to the party once again. The knights have one target here: Overlord Drakuru, whom they have followed since the Grizzly Hills.

parts.body: A choker of bone found on a dead troll compels whoever finds it to serve the Scourge, and is never wasted on a random target. Stefan turned the snare around into a disguise to walk among the Scourge.

title: Voltarus
body: Over the blighted pools of northwestern Zul'Drak hang two necropolises. Voltarus hovers above the Reliquary of Pain, where blight geists harvest crystals of blight and abominations lurch among blight cauldrons, and it is the seat of Overlord Drakuru. To the southwest Zeramas hangs over the Reliquary of Agony. North of Voltarus, at the Frigid Breach, a Drakkari army has broken through the wall.

parts.body: In an upper chamber stand Drakuru's secret weapons: Blightblood trolls, the makings of the ultimate Scourge army with which he means to take the palace of Gundrak.

title: Overlord Drakuru
body: Overlord Drakuru commands the Scourge in Zul'Drak from the necropolis Voltarus. He is a Drakkari himself, and by his own orders the Lich King has given him full control of the Scourge's armies here. The trolls who follow him call themselves the Drakuru, and he promises that he will soon drink the blood of the prophets and see Zul'Drak and Gundrak fall.

parts.body: To those who helped him in the Grizzly Hills he speaks as an old friend: the choker that called them to Voltarus was his gift, and now they serve the Lich King side by side.
sources: quest 12883 description (Orders From Drakuru)

parts.body: His trust was his undoing. His Blightbloods were turned against him, and the Lich King came, but only to condemn him for his failure and strike him dead.

title: Altar of Sseratus
body: At the end of the avenue north of the Argent Stand rises the Altar of Sseratus, the snake god's holy place. Its priests and champions still crowd the steps, and a prophet holds court before the main building, boasting that with the power of the wild gods in their veins not even the Lich King can stand against them.

parts.body: Inside lies Sseratus, slain by his own worshippers, who have drunk deeply of his mojo, the prophet most of all.

title: Zim'Torga
body: Up the great steps on the next tier of the city lies Zim'Torga, a refuge the Zandalari have taken beneath the statue of the Mother of Prosperity, come from Zandalar to defend the gods who still live. Around them altar after altar has fallen: the snow leopard goddess Har'koa is held by her own subduers, the bear god Rhunok is kept close to death, and something is wrong at the altar of the wind serpent.

parts.body: Rather than let his trolls drink his power, the mammoth god Mam'toth destroyed himself and much of his temple with him, leaving a crater where his blood still lives.
sources: quest 12623 description (Zim'Torga up the great steps to the northeast; refuge the Zandalari defend; constant attack)

parts.body: Having given part of her spirit so that Quetz'lun could be avenged, Har'koa left her altar and now dwells in the Zandalari refuge.

title: Gundrak
body: Gundrak is the capital of the Drakkari Empire, a great palace city whose trolls swarm its approaches. In the courtyard before its gates Akali, the rhino god, lies in chains at four anchor points while his subduers prepare him for slaughter. Beside the city a few Zandalari keep watch from Dubra'Jin, observing and recording what they see.

parts.body: Akali was freed, and at once his prophet slew him, claiming his blood for his master and some of his power for himself, and swore he was coming for Har'koa next.
